memory_candidates.content: When applying a cross-repository documentation hand-off (one repo's task derives copy-ready replacement text for another repo's docs without crossing the boundary), don't transcribe the hand-off note's prose verbatim even when it looks copy-ready. Independently re-verify every cited declaration name and every substantive proof-shape claim against the live source tree first: a hand-off note can be stale relative to its own repository (e.g. it may describe a route via file X when the landed proof actually uses a differently-named, differently-located transcription of that route), and re-deriving from the live tree catches this before it's written into a durable document. A repository's own research-report artifact (produced ahead of the plan/implement phases) is often a better source than the upstream note itself, since it was written specifically to the target document's exact current structure and style constraints.
